features.title: Board
features.body: The podium, weekly and streak rankings, and your pace to the next level

features.title: Titles
features.body: Competitive titles in categories, from longest streak to night runs. Pick the ones you show On display

features.title: Badges
features.body: Eight series with six tiers each, collected across seasons. Pick up to three on the Badges page to show on the Board and your Runner card

features.title: Duels
features.body: 1v1 challenges with tokens earned at level-up. Send one in a few taps, the winner gets a boost

features.title: Events
features.body: Daily time windows, weekly competitions and Storm Chaser on real forecasts, with a live countdown

features.title: Log runs
features.body: See your Estimated XP before you save, and what the run does to your streak

features.title: Profile
features.body: Your stats, a heatmap of your running and Frodo's Journey with three zoom levels

features.title: Runner card
features.body: Tap anyone to see their level, titles and head-to-head record with you

features.title: Pack News
features.body: Everything the group does in one feed, with filters, an Involves me view and a bell that shows what is new

features.title: Notifications
features.body: Choose what the bell counts and what its list shows, in Settings → Notifications or on the Pack News page

features.title: Playbook
features.body: The full game rules: XP, multipliers, levels, titles and tokens

features.title: Phone and desktop
features.body: Bottom navigation on your phone, a side menu on desktop

workingOn.title: Seasons and trophies
workingOn.body: Play in seasons, with a level of their own and a cabinet for what you win

workingOn.title: Group settings
workingOn.body: Each group gets settings of its own, so the rules can differ between groups

changes.description: Notifications you control: in Settings → Notifications, or on the Pack News page, switch on what the bell counts and what its list shows, from titles taken from you to rank changes. Pack News itself always shows everything.
Mark news as read one row at a time: move your mouse over a row, tap it, or press Enter or Space. Tabbing onto a row does not count as reading it. Mark all read is still there.

Pack News has an Involves me button that keeps only news about you: your moves, moves against you and events you joined. The new Ranks filter shows when someone passes you on the leaderboard or the challenge standings, and you get a note when someone accepts your challenge.

Connecting Strava now starts with a short summary you tick to agree to: what is imported, what happens when you delete a run on Strava, that Disconnect deletes your Strava runs, and that you can pause sync. The full text is in Privacy & Terms.

In Settings you can Pause sync (your connection and runs stay, but no new runs are fetched until you turn sync back on; the new runs from the pause are fetched when you turn it back on) or Disconnect. Disconnect asks Strava to revoke RunQuest's access and deletes the runs imported from Strava, and it cannot be undone. Runs you added by hand stay.
The start page is rebuilt for people who haven't joined yet: what RunQuest is, a 49-second film, real numbers from the app (km, runners and challenges), how XP works and what's in the game.
Friends who want in can join a waitlist on the start page. They get an invite when a pack can start. No email is sent yet.
New page Privacy & Terms (linked at the bottom of the start page) explains what RunQuest stores, who sees it and how to have it removed.
Sign in now sits at the top right of the start page. Shared links to RunQuest show a proper preview with title and image.
Pack News has a Badges filter of its own, right after Levels. Badges no longer show up under Levels.
New versions of RunQuest now show up in Pack News too, so you can see what changed even if you closed the What's new popup.

Badges are here: eight series, six tiers from Common to Legendary, collected across seasons. They have their own page: on a wide screen open Badges in the side menu; on your phone tap All badges → on your Profile. Each card shows what it takes to reach the next tier.
Pick up to three badges to show on the Board and your Runner card: tap Show on a badge, then SAVE DISPLAY. A popup tells you when you reach a new tier, and Pack News tells the group.

Three new titles in a new Weather category: Stormborn (most runs in gusts of 12 m/s or more, about 43 km/h), Iceborn (most runs at 5 °C or colder) and Winter Warrior (most km in December to February). Playbook explains how the winter is counted, and when a new winter starts.
Your Profile and every Runner card show badges as a compact row you can tap to see the tier and what it takes. On a wide screen the Runner card row sits next to Head to head.
Signing in now opens as a popup over the start page, and Log out takes you back to the start page.
Challenge tokens are now small pennants instead of shields, on the Board and in Duels.

Runs imported from Strava are read-only in RunQuest, since distance and date come from Strava. Early Bird and Night Owl badges go by the clock where you ran, and 'x h ago' on the Board is no longer an hour or two off for runs in Sweden.

releases.title: Storm Chaser needs a real storm

changes.description: Storm Chaser now only comes up for properly rough weather: at least three hours of rain, snow or thunder, or four hours of gusts of 15 m/s (about 54 km/h). Before, a light breeze was enough.
The small capital labels above headings are easier to read.

releases.title: The new look reaches the rest of the app

changes.description: Playbook, Settings and the sign-in page now have the new RunQuest look.
Playbook shows the XP rules that are live right now, so what you read is what you earn.
Feature & Version and this What's new window have a fresh layout.

releases.title: Smoother updates, news dot and all your titles

changes.description: Fixed a blank white page that could appear after an update. The app now picks up new versions by itself, with no cache clearing needed. If you still see the old page, reload once.
Unread Pack News has a gold dot, on the time, in the feed and in the bell.
On your phone, the Board shows every title a runner has on display (up to three) under their name, on every rank, and from 4th place down the cards show level and XP progress like the podium.
A brand-new look: a dark arena where gold means reward. Bottom navigation on your phone, a side menu on desktop, and a new start page for visitors.
Runner card: tap anyone to see their level, stats, titles and head-to-head record, with a Challenge button.
Titles come in categories, with On display to choose the ones you show off and Closest chase to see what is within reach.
Duels: pick a token, pick an opponent and see the stakes before you send.
Events open with a live countdown, and Log runs shows your Estimated XP before you save.
Profile has a heatmap of your running and Frodo's Journey with three zoom levels.
Pack News: a feed of everything the group does, with a bell that shows what is new.
Public profiles — tap any leaderboard card, group run history name or challenge opponent to open their full profile in a modal. Shows stats, Frodo's Journey progress and titles.
Scheduled events now appear in the sidebar widget with the same coming-soon countdown overlay as pending challenges.
Onboarding system — interactive feature tours guide new members through the leaderboard, challenges, events and profile page step by step.
Patch notes — new features trigger an in-app notification so you always know what changed. Full release history on the Features page.
Frodo's Journey expanded with 24 new Tolkien waypoints (Weathertop, Lothlórien, Cirith Ungol and more) and a three-level zoom function to see your local progress in detail.
Journey moved to its own full-width card directly below the profile header for better visibility.

Events system — app-wide challenges that trigger automatically on a schedule or based on real weather. Two types: Participation (earn XP by running within a time window) and Competition (weekly ranking by total km or elevation).

Five participation events: Morning run (06:00–10:00), Evening run (18:00–22:00), 5K Friday, Hangover Run (weekends), and Storm Chaser — only triggered when tomorrow's forecast shows rain, drizzle, thunderstorm or strong gusts.
Two weekly competition events: Weekly km and Weekly höjdmeter — ranking everyone in the group, settled Sunday at 23:55 with XP awarded per place (40/30/20).
Events page — shows active and upcoming events, live competition leaderboard, and full history with per-event results and group completion status.
Event widgets in the sidebar — active participation events show a countdown to close, competition events show your current rank. Upcoming events show a countdown to open.
Playbook updated with an Events tab explaining all event types, rules, XP values, and how Storm Chaser weather detection works.
UI changes for Run history - group. You can now clearly see how the XP is gained.
Playbook page — full game rules documentation covering XP formula, streak multipliers, levels, titles and challenge tokens. Accessible from the sidebar.
Profile page redesigned — stats and run history now in a proper two-column layout that fills the full viewport height on desktop.
Run history pagination is now dynamic — the number of cards per page adapts automatically to the available height so the list always fills the panel without overflow.

Frodo Journey updated — The Shire and MORDOR are now shown below the bar, intermediate checkpoints (Bree, Rivendell, Moria, Rauros, The Black Gate) are above at alternating heights with connecting tick lines.
Streak multiplier displayed on the profile stats page now reflects the actual value stored per run (calculated by the backend with live DB settings) instead of a hardcoded frontend approximation.
Weather data is now saved for every outdoor run — temperature, feels-like, humidity, wind speed and gusts, precipitation, snowfall, snow depth, UV index and visibility.
Data is fetched automatically after Strava sync using the run's GPS coordinates and start time via Open-Meteo — no setup required.
Historical weather is also backfilled for older runs that have location data, so your full run history gets enriched over time.
Foundation for upcoming weather-based titles and challenges — run in the rain, wind or snow and let it count.
Runs are now tagged as treadmill or outdoor — detected automatically from Strava's trainer flag.
Titles and stats that require outdoor running correctly exclude treadmill sessions — no more indoor runs inflating outdoor achievements.
Backfill applied to all existing Strava runs so historical data is accurate from day one.
Challenge system — players earn challenge tokens when leveling up and can send them to group members as 1v1 challenges.
Three challenge tiers: Minor (5–7 days), Major (7–14 days) and Legendary (14–30 days) — each with different metrics (km, runs, XP) and reward multipliers.
Winner gets an XP multiplier boost, loser takes a penalty — challenges are settled automatically when the time window closes.
Challenges page — view active challenges, pending requests, history and a W/D/L leaderboard for the group.
Active challenge widget in the top bar — shows live score and days remaining, links directly to the challenge page.
Leaderboard now shows tier flags (tokens ready to send) and a swords icon for users currently in an active challenge.
Dark mode — toggle between light and dark theme from the sidebar or top bar. RunQuest defaults to your system theme and remembers your preference.
Full design rework — consistent color hierarchy across all pages using theme-aware tokens. Outer containers use sidebar color, inner elements use background color.
Sidebar redesigned — Strava sync status with last/next sync times, mobile controls (theme toggle, notifications, profile) moved into the sidebar.
Leaderboard cards redesigned — compact layout, fixed 340px width, centered podium row, positions 4+ fill rows from center outward.
Profile page redesigned — two-column layout with run history as a right panel, avatar and position in the card header, streak stats beside the profile card.
Run history now uses pagination (7 runs per page) with previous/next navigation instead of a growing list.
Mobile optimizations — group name wraps correctly in the top bar, profile and streak cards stack vertically on small screens.
Cleaned up behind the scenes — the app now makes fewer unnecessary requests and loads data faster.
Faster startup and more stable performance during use.
Fixed a bug in the title system that could occasionally show incorrect data on page load.
Session is now automatically restored when login needs to be renewed — no more manual cookie clearing.
You stay logged in for 30 days instead of 7.
Leaderboard with XP, levels, streaks and titles.
Four competitive titles that update automatically.
Run logging — manually or via Strava.
User profiles with profile picture and personal stats.
Admin panel for user and XP management.
